description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy metrics for a model on TriviaQA, displaying three distinct measures: Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, ranging from 0.71 to 1.00 in linear scale, with tick labels spaced approximately every 0.02. The y-axis represents Accuracy, scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line with circular markers and solid style represents Final Accuracy, starting at approximately 0.95, peaking near 1.00 at an initial confidence of 0.79, then generally declining to about 0.90 by the end of the range. The green line with square markers and dashed style represents Initial Accuracy, beginning near 0.55, rising to a peak of approximately 0.90 at an initial confidence of 0.79, then showing a decline to around 0.80 by the end. The orange line with diamond markers and dash-dotted style represents Δ Accuracy, starting at approximately 0.35, dropping sharply to near 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.73, then exhibiting a fluctuating pattern with peaks around 0.40 and troughs near 0.05 throughout the remaining range.
